data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's central formalization of 'safe' as requiring an 'empty set of state transitions' / 'null effect' misrepresents RFC 9110's actual definition. RFC 9110 §9.2.1 defines safe methods as methods that do not produce actions beyond retrieval for which the user is accountable — not methods with zero server-side state transitions. The standard explicitly notes that safe methods can still have side effects on the server (e.g., logging, caching). Because SRC_001's entire argument that 'safety forbids the very operation (state mutation) the log exists to perform' hinges on this null-transition mischaracterization, it fails to ground the distinction in the published definition the problem asks for. The target even self-flags this in a countercondition ('If RFC 9110's definitions are not set-theoretic in this way and the formalization is an imposed overlay, it may not match the standard's actual language'), conceding that its formalization may not correspond to the standard's real language — yet it builds its substantive conclusion on that unverified overlay.
